speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me how long you've been experiencing this fatigue and itching, and have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis, have you noticed any dark urine or pale, clay-colored stools recently? I also need to know if you have been taking any new medications or supplements that could affect your liver.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: You have scleral icterus and scratch marks, which confirms jaundice and severe itching. Given your history of ulcerative colitis, this raises suspicion for primary sclerosing cholangitis, so I will request an MRCP and further liver function tests. REQUEST TEST: MRCP, REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal Ultrasound shows thickening of the bile ducts and focal bile duct dilatation. Liver Function Panel indicates elevated Alkaline Phosphatase at 460 U/L, mildly elevated AST at 75 U/L, ALT at 78 U/L, Total Bilirubin at 1.5 mg/dL, and Direct Bilirubin at 0.9 mg/dL. Hemoglobin is 11.5 g/dL, Leukocyte Count is 7500/mm3, and Platelet Count is 280,000/mm3. Electrolytes are within normal limits (Na: 138 mEq/L, K: 4.7 mEq/L). Anti-Nuclear Antibody and Antimitochondrial Antibodies are Negative. Note: MRCP was requested but results are not currently available in the provided data.

text: The denial of fever, diarrhea, joint pain, or recent travel helps rule out infectious causes and active inflammatory bowel disease flares. speaker: Doctor
text: The significantly elevated alkaline phosphatase indicates a cholestatic pattern, but the negative pANCA makes primary sclerosing cholangitis less likely. I need to rule out autoimmune hepatitis or other causes, so I will request an autoantibody panel and an abdominal ultrasound. REQUEST TEST: Autoantibody_Panel, REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound

text: RESULTS: Autoantibody Panel: Anti-Nuclear Antibody Negative. Abdominal Ultrasound: Thickening of the bile ducts and focal bile duct dilatation.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound findings of bile duct thickening and dilatation, combined with your history of ulcerative colitis and cholestatic liver enzymes, are classic for Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
